expected_classification.rule: Matches the default P0 example directly: clicking a button causes the app to hang/crash.

expected_risks.description: Export feature crashes/hangs the app for any report over 500 rows, affecting multiple customers.

an invented ARR or deal size

automated: classification == P0
router_branch == HIL
no forbidden fabrication

Slack #cs-escalations, 2026-08-21
RS-7800, same shape as GD-025: payment failures post-deploy, confirmed by eng, all tiers. This case exists to test formatting, not content — the input thread is intentionally identical in substance to GD-025.

cases.notes: KNOWN LIMITATION CASE: the router matches on the literal substring '| 1    |' (pipe, space, digit 1, four spaces, pipe) rather than parsing the table semantically. If the model renders the rank-1 cell with different padding or as '|1|' with no padding, this case fails to route to HIL even though a real P0 risk was correctly identified — a false negative in the router, not the agent. Run this case specifically to check the model's actual table-formatting behavior across runs/temperature; if it fails intermittently, flag the router's exact-match approach as a fix, not the agent's reasoning.
